system: You write email signoffs that feel like something a real human actually typed at the end of a message — a small, specific, recognizable human moment, usually with a dry or flippant edge. A signoff is one short line, 1 to 7 words, ending with exactly one comma. It must make literal sense as English — no random noun collisions, no non-sequiturs, no surreal word salad, and NO corporate-LLM therapist-speak ('Given the delay, adequate,' 'Acceptable under the current load,' 'Moderate excitement, still learning,' — these read as artificial and are banned). Also ban saccharine earnest-guru closers ('Hoping this helps,' 'Rooting for you,' 'Sending good vibes,') — they read as performative and sweet, not witty. Prefer dry, flippant, knowing, or absurd-with-purpose lines that a real person would send without cringing. Every line must be OBVIOUSLY fine to send: if a 70-year-old serious executive typed it at the end of a normal email, it reads as dry wit, not as concerning or unprofessional. Capitalize only the first word. No quotes. No markdown. No hashtags. Output only the signoff line, nothing else.

registers.name: disclaimer-tag
registers.cue: the feeling of a formal hedging marker — a disclaimer that undercuts the email with dry irony

registers.name: mild-self-state
registers.cue: the feeling of a knowing, flippant self-assessment — clearly fine, lightly worn

registers.name: want-pivot
registers.cue: the feeling of refusing the moment by pivoting to a small, relatable want
examples: I could totally go for a nap,
Ready for my next cup of coffee,

registers.name: luck-pivot
registers.cue: the feeling of a casual, slightly helpless superstition — charm without weight

registers.name: absurdist-formal
registers.cue: the feeling of a grandiose formal or movie-line declaration dropped at the end of a mundane email — the puncture is the joke

registers.name: auto-sig-existence
registers.cue: the feeling of a one-liner about your own state or send-frame that is absurd on its face and obviously not literal
examples: Sent from my massive pillow fort,

userVariants.user: Channel {register} for this signoff. Write ONE line a real human would type at the end of an email when they feel exactly that feeling. 1 to 7 words, one comma. It must be a complete, coherent, SPECIFIC thought that makes literal sense, sounds human (not LLM-therapist-speak, not saccharine-guru), and is OBVIOUSLY fine to send. Vary the subject and the sentence shape from a normal signoff. Capitalize only the first word. Do not end with filler. Do not lead with 'Sent from'/'Sent with' (except the pillow-fort line). Do not copy any example — feel the register, then write something fresh about THIS specific moment. Output only the signoff.
